messages:
Maria Chen: quick question — compliance flagged that customers expect verifiable audit receipts for Private deployments (VPC/on-prem). They want a way to validate that events were recorded and retained immutable for their retention window. Thoughts?

Sanjay Patel: Are they asking for signed receipts per event or a periodic signed manifest? Per-event signing is heavy, manifests with Merkle roots might be better.

Carlos Rivera: Agree. Proposal: we include per-day manifest that contains SHA256 for each event file + KMS-signed manifest signature. That keeps per-event size small but provides cryptographic proof.

Olivia Grant: Need to ensure KMS usage is compatible with customer-managed keys (CMKs) in Private. If customer supplies key, we must not be able to re-sign after key rotation without customer involvement.

Maria Chen: Right — and for Hosted/Dedicated customers we could use Redwood-managed keys but expose signed receipts endpoint.

Sanjay Patel: On the schema side, we'll add metadata fields: event_id, file_path, seq_no, event_hash, key_id, retention_policy_id, immutability_epoch.

Carlos Rivera: Sample event snippet:
```
{"event_id":"evt_3f9a","ts":"2026-12-02T14:23:11Z","actor":"svc-redwood","action":"model.deploy","resource":"model:abc","event_hash":"e3b0c44298fc1c14..."}
```

Olivia Grant: For WORM compliance, S3 Object Lock + Governance mode + KMS-managed encryption is fine for cloud. For on-prem we need an append-only store with signed manifests and HSM timestamping.

Jules Kim: From vuln triage: make sure signing path can't be abused. Do not accept arbitrary inputs into manifest builder. Also rotate signing keys and keep audit of key usage.

Maria Chen: Incident scenario — if an attacker deletes live events but not manifests, how do we prove tamper? We need proofs that bind manifest to raw events (hash chain) and store manifests in multiple locations (cold archival + notarization service).

Sanjay Patel: Also add replay-resistant nonces in manifests. Keep manifest per-hour for high-volume tenants, daily for low-volume.

Olivia Grant: Customer-facing validation API concept: POST /audit/verify with: {receipt_id, manifest_sig, proof_path}, returns {valid:true,hash_match:true,retention_ok:true} 

Carlos Rivera: Need to define retention policy lifecycle header: `x-retention-policy: "r:365d;mode:worm;key:kms:arn:..."` — that'll be in event/file metadata.

Maria Chen: Action items:
- Sanjay: draft schema PR with new fields + example events (due EOD Thu)
- Carlos: prototype manifest signer with KMS + HSM fallback (P0)
- Olivia: confirm on-prem HSM signing requirements with infra (sync Fri)
- Jules: threat model for signing + manifest ingestion (next week)

Maria Chen: Thanks — tagging @audit-bot to record thread

audit-bot: Recorded: compliance_request_5793 by Maria Chen at 1792345678 :thumbsup:

Sanjay Patel: I pushed an initial schema to git: https://git.internal/r/audit/schemas/merge/39 — pls comment

Olivia Grant: Quick note — we must update RBAC so only audit-service roles can read raw events; support read-only 'audit-reader' role for customers with limited fields exposed.

Carlos Rivera: Also consider encrypting per-event payload with data key and storing DEKs encrypted with customer KMS for Private. For Hosted, default to Redwood KMS with option to bring-your-own.

Maria Chen: OK, next sync Tuesday to review proofs prototype. Thanks all :handshake:
